questions.q: Which bond is submitted with a bid to guarantee that the contractor will enter into a contract if they are selected as the winner?
questions.n: This bond provides financial assurance to the owner that the successful bidder will sign the contract and provide the required performance and payment bonds.

questions.q: What bond protects the owner from financial loss if the contractor fails to complete the project according to the plans and specifications?
questions.n: It guarantees that the project will be finished according to the agreed-upon quality and timeline stated in the contract.

questions.q: Which bond ensures that the contractor will pay all subcontractors, laborers, and material suppliers involved in the project?
questions.n: Also known as a labor and material bond, it prevents the owner from being liable for the contractor's debts to third parties.

questions.q: What is the term for the bond that guarantees the contractor will correct any defects in workmanship or materials for a specific period after completion?
questions.n: Also called a Maintenance Bond, it typically covers a period of one year to ensure any 'latent defects' are addressed at no cost to the owner.

questions.q: If a contractor requests an initial payment before work starts to buy materials, what bond might the owner require to protect that specific advance?
questions.n: It ensures that if the contractor fails to utilize the down payment for the project, the owner can recoup the funds.

questions.q: What is the primary permit required before any construction, alteration, or repair of a building can begin under the NBC?
questions.n: This is the 'mother' permit that signifies the plans comply with the National Building Code and local regulations.

questions.q: Which permit must be secured before any 'land-clearing' or 'earth-moving' activities on the site?
questions.n: This accessory permit is required to ensure that digging does not affect the stability of adjacent properties or public utilities.

questions.q: Before structural framing begins, which permit is required for the installation of temporary electrical lines used during construction?
questions.n: This allows the contractor to have safe, metered power for tools and site lighting during the build process.

questions.q: If the project requires the installation of a perimeter fence to secure the site, what specific accessory permit must be applied for?
questions.n: It ensures the fence height and material comply with safety and aesthetic standards set by the code.

questions.q: What document must be secured from the local government unit (LGU) to ensure the proposed building is allowed in that specific zone?
questions.n: This confirms that the project's use (e.g., residential vs. industrial) aligns with the city's Comprehensive Land Use Plan.

questions.q: The Rietveld Schröder House is famous for its use of 'Primary Colors.' What are these three colors as defined by the De Stijl movement?
o: Earth tones like Brown and Tan
questions.n: These colors, combined with black and white, were intended to represent the essence of the universe through abstraction.

questions.q: What is the term for the 'open' and 'transformable' floor plan on the upper floor of the Rietveld Schröder House?
questions.n: The upper floor can be converted from a single open area into several private rooms using movable partitions.

questions.q: The exterior of the house is characterized by the 'interpenetration' of what type of geometric elements?
questions.n: The house appears as a series of floating slabs and slender beams that seem to slide past one another.

questions.q: Who is the architect and furniture designer responsible for the Rietveld Schröder House?
questions.n: He was a leading member of the De Stijl movement and also designed the iconic Red and Blue Chair.

questions.q: The house rejects 'enclosed' rooms. What is the name of the theory that views architecture as a composition of floating volumes?
questions.n: Also known as 'Nieuwe Beelding,' it sought to express a new utopian ideal through pure geometric forms and primary colors.

questions.q: Which principle states that the design should be useful and marketable to people with diverse abilities?
questions.n: It means the design provides the same means of use for all users: identical whenever possible; equivalent when not.

questions.q: What principle requires the design to accommodate a wide range of individual preferences and abilities (e.g., right- or left-handed use)?
questions.n: This principle allows for choice in methods of use, such as an ambidextrous pair of scissors or a height-adjustable desk.

questions.q: What ensures the design communicates necessary information effectively, regardless of sensory abilities?
questions.n: This principle ensures that instructions or signals are clear to everyone, including those with visual or hearing impairments.

questions.q: Which principle focuses on minimizing hazards and the adverse consequences of accidental actions?
questions.n: Design elements should be arranged to minimize hazards: the most used elements are most accessible; hazardous elements are eliminated or shielded.

questions.q: In the context of accessibility, what is the maximum allowable gradient for a ramp according to BP 344?
questions.n: This means for every 1 unit of vertical height, you must have at least 12 units of horizontal length.

questions.q: Constructing without a permit is generally classified under which category of violation?
questions.n: Because it bypasses the safety review and inspections required by the state, it is considered a major offense against public safety.

questions.q: Failure to post the 'Building Permit' or 'Excavation Permit' in a conspicuous place is typically what type of violation?
questions.n: This is a failure in the 'posting' requirement—a minor administrative error that does not necessarily mean the plans are unsafe.

questions.q: What type of violation is committed when there is a 'deviation' from the approved plans without prior approval?
questions.n: As long as the deviation doesn't immediately endanger the building, it's considered less grave until the plans are corrected.

questions.q: Non-compliance with the 'Use/Occupancy' requirements is classified as what?
questions.n: A residential building may not have the fire exits or load capacity required for a commercial business, making misuse a 'Grave' danger.

questions.q: If a contractor fails to provide safety catch-fans or protective nets, what is the classification of this safety violation?
questions.n: Failure to provide fall protection and debris containment is a direct threat to the lives of both workers and the public.
